source_text: Τοιουτότροπον γὰρ καὶ ἄλλο εἴρηται τῷ αὐτῷ προφήτῃ ἀπὸ τοῦ δεσποτικοῦ προσώπου· «τίς ὁ κρινόμενός μοι; ἀντιστήτω μοι· καὶ τίς ὁ κρινόμενός μοι; ἐγγισάτω μοι»· ἀντὶ τοῦ· εἴ τις ἔχει δίκαια λέγειν, ὡς ἔργοις ὠχυρωμένος, ἀντενεχθήτω μοι θέλοντι τοῦτο καὶ πλησιασάτω τοῖς λόγοις. 28.16 ἔνιοι δὲ ἀναγινώσκουσι τοιῶσδε· «τίς ὁ κρινόμενός μοι; ἀντί» τοῦτ' ἔστι καταντικρὺ καὶ πόρρω που «στήτω μου» ὡς μὴ ἔχων ἐφόδια καλὰ καὶ διὰ τοῦτο συγκριθῆναί μοι καὶ ἐπιψαῦσαι τοῦ καθαρωτάτου βήματος ἀνάξιος. 28.17 τοῖς γὰρ ἀξίοις, εἰ τυγχάνοιεν τῶν καλῶν, οὐδεὶς φθόνος· αὐτοῖς γὰρ ἡτοίμασται. 29.ν Περὶ τοῦ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ εἶναι «κριτὴν ζώντων καὶ νεκρῶν» ἄφεσιν ἁμαρ τιῶν παρέχοντα, καὶ ὅτι «ἐν οὐδενὶ ἄλλῳ ἐστὶν ἡ σωτηρία». 29.1 Αὐτὸς γάρ ἐστιν «ὁ κριτὴς ζώντων καὶ νεκρῶν», τουτέστιν δικαίων καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν, ὁ παρέχων ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν τοῖς πιστεύουσιν τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ καὶ σώζων ἡμᾶς ἰδίᾳ δόξῃ καὶ δωρεᾷ. 29.2 καί «ἐν οὐδενὶ ἄλλῳ ἐστὶν σωτηρία», ἐπείπερ τὴν φύσιν ἐστὶν ἵλεως καὶ σωτήρ, εἰς οὐδὲν καταδεέστερος τοῦ ἵλεω καὶ σώζοντος θεοῦ καὶ πατρός, ὡς χρησμῳδοῦσιν αἵ τε ἄλλαι γραφαὶ καὶ μέντοι Μιχαίας λέγων· «τίς θεὸς ὥσπερ σὺ ἐξαίρων ἀνομίας καὶ ὑπερβαίνων ἀδικίας;» 29.3 Καὶ Πέτρος ἐν ταῖς πράξεσιν οὑτωσί· «καὶ παρήγγειλεν ἡμῖν κηρύξαι τῷ λαῷ καὶ διαμαρτύρασθαι, ὅτι αὐτός ἐστιν ὁ ὡρισμένος ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ κριτὴς ζώντων καὶ νεκρῶν. τούτῳ πάντες οἱ προ φῆται μαρτυροῦσιν, ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν λαβεῖν διὰ τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ πάντα τὸν πιστεύοντα εἰς αὐτόν». 29.4 Ἔχομεν αὐτὸν τοίνυν εὐφημηθέντα, ὡρισμένον ὑπὸ 34 θεοῦ διὰ τὴν σωτήριον ἐνανθρώπησιν αὐτοῦ, ἐν ᾗ ἦλθεν «ζητῆσαι καὶ σῶσαι τὸ ἀπολωλός». δι' ἣν καὶ τό «οὐδὲ γὰρ ὁ πατὴρ κρίνει οὐδένα, ἀλλὰ πᾶσαν τὴν κρίσιν δέδωκεν τῷ υἱῷ» γέγραπται· 29.5 κριτὴν δὲ ὡς ἐξῃρημένον τῶν κτισμάτων. 29.6 τὸ γὰρ κτίσμα οὐ κρίνει, ἀλλὰ νόμῳ καὶ κρίσει ὑπόκειται. 29.7 Καὶ πάλιν· «οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ λίθος ὁ ἐξουδενωθεὶς ὑφ' ὑμῶν τῶν οἰκοδόμων, ὁ γενόμενος εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας. καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν ἄλλῳ οὐδενὶ ἡ σωτηρία». 29.8 Ἀλλὰ καὶ καθολικὰ τὸ δεύτερον πέμπει γράμματα, μεταξὺ ἄλλων περὶ αὐτοῦ ἔχοντα καὶ τοῦτο· «ὡς τὰ πάντα ἡμῖν τῆς θείας δυνάμεως αὐτοῦ τὰ πρὸς ζωὴν καὶ εὐσέβειαν δεδωρημένης διὰ τῆς ἐπιγνώσεως τοῦ καλέσαντος ἡμᾶς ἰδίᾳ δόξῃ καὶ ἀρε τῇ, δι' ὧν τὰ μέγιστα καὶ τίμια ἡμῖν εὐαγγέλματα δεδώρηται, ἵνα διὰ τού των γένησθε θείας κοινωνοὶ φύσεως». 29.9 ∆ιὸ καὶ Ἰάκωβος ἐν γενικοῖς χαράγμασιν ἔφη· «εἷς ἐστιν ὁ νομοθέτης καὶ κριτής, ὁ δυνάμενος σῶσαι καὶ ἀπολέσαι». 29.10 Τί δὲ πλήθους δεῖ γραφῶν εἰς τοῦτο λοιπόν; καὶ Σαμαρειτῶν παρὰ Ἰωάννῃ τῷ ἀκριβεῖ θεηγόρῳ, εὐγνωμόνων ἀνδρῶν, ἀφιέντων φωνάς· «αὐτοὶ γάρ», φησίν, «ἀκηκόαμεν καὶ οἴδαμεν, ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ἀληθῶς ὁ σωτὴρ τοῦ κόσμου, ὁ Χριστός», ὁ λέγων, φησίν, ἠπίως· «θάρσει, τέκνον, ἀφέωνταί σοι αἱ ἁμαρτίαι». 30.ν Περὶ τοῦ διὰ τὴν ἰσοτιμίαν τῆς τριάδος τὸν πατέρα ἀποκαλύπτειν ἡμῖν τὸν υἱὸν καὶ ἕλκειν ἡμᾶς πρὸς αὐτόν, καὶ πάλιν αὐτὸν υἱὸν καὶ τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα προσάγειν ἡμᾶς τῷ πατρί. ἐν ταὐτῷ καὶ περὶ τῆς ὁμολογίας Πέτρου, καὶ ὅτι ἔστιν μετάνοια. 30.1 Ἵνα γὰρ δι' ὅλων ἀποδειχθῇ τῆς μακαρίας τριάδος τὸ περὶ πάντα ἰσότιμον, ἀποκαλύπτει ἡμῖν τὸν ἴδιον υἱὸν ὁ πατὴρ καὶ ἕλκει ἡμᾶς δι' ἑαυτοῦ πρὸς αὐτὸν καὶ μεθιστᾷ εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν αὐτοῦ· 30.2 καὶ πάλιν ὁ υἱὸς καὶ τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα προσάγει ἡμᾶς τῷ θεῷ καὶ πατρί. 30.3 οὐκ ἂν γὰρ εἰς ἑτεροούσιον ἢ μείζονα οὐδ' εἰς ὑποκατερχόμενα ὥσπερ σκῆπτρα τῶν ἑαυτοῦ μετέθηκεν ἡμᾶς ὁ θεός. 30.4 τετελείωκεν γοῦν τὴν παλαιὰν διαθήκην ἡ νέα διὰ τὴν εἰς τὸν υἱὸν καὶ τὸ θεῖον πνεῦμα πίστιν. 30.5 Λέγουσι δὲ ὧδε ὁ μὲν θεὸς πατὴρ ἐν Ἠσαΐᾳ πρὸς τὸν υἱόν· «ἰδοὺ προσήλυτοι προσελεύσονταί σοι δι' ἐμοῦ καὶ παροικήσουσίν σοι καὶ ἐπὶ σοὶ καταφεύξονται»· 30.6 ὁ δὲ υἱὸς ἐν Ἰωάννῃ· «οὐδεὶς δύναται ἐλθεῖν πρός με, ἐὰν μὴ ὁ πατὴρ ὁ οὐράνιος ἑλκύσῃ αὐτόν, κἀγὼ ἀναστήσω αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρα». 30.7 καὶ πάλιν πρὸς τὸν Πέτρον εἰπόντα «σὺ εἶ ὁ Χριστός, ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ζῶντος» ἔφη· «μακάριος εἶ, Πέτρε βὰρ Ἰωνᾶ, ὅτι σὰρξ καὶ αἷμα οὐκ ἀπεκάλυψέν σοι, ἀλλ' ὁ πατήρ μου ὁ ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς. κἀγὼ δέ σοι λέγω, ὅτι σὺ εἶ Πέτρος, καὶ ἐπὶ ταύτῃ τῇ πέτρᾳ οἰκοδομήσω μου τὴν ἐκκλησίαν, καὶ πῦλαι ᾅδου οὐ κατισχύ σουσιν αὐτῆς. καὶ δώσω σοι τὰς κλεῖς τῶν οὐρανῶν, καὶ ὃ ἐὰν δήσῃς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ἔσται δεδεμένον ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς, καὶ ὃ ἐὰν λύσῃς ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ἔσται λελυμένον ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς». 30.8
pass_a_gloss: 28.15 For of such a kind another thing too has been said by the same prophet from the Master's person: 'who is the one going to law with me? let him stand against me; and who is the one going to law with me? let him draw near to me'; in place of [saying]: if anyone has just things to say, as fortified by works, let him be brought against me, who wish this, and let him draw near with the words. 28.16 But some read thus: 'who is the one going to law with me? against', that is, right opposite and somewhere far off, 'let him stand from me', as not having good provisions for the road and for this reason unworthy to be compared with me and to touch the most pure judgment seat. 28.17 For to the worthy, if they should obtain the good things, there is no grudging; for it has been prepared for them. 29.ν [Chapter title:] About the Son of God being 'judge of living and dead', providing forgiveness of sins, and that 'in no one else is the salvation'. 29.1 For he himself is 'the judge of living and dead', that is, of righteous and sinners, the one providing forgiveness of sins to those who believe in his name and saving us by his own glory and gift. 29.2 And 'in no one else is there salvation', since by nature he is merciful and Saviour, in nothing more lacking than the merciful and saving God and Father, as the other Scriptures declare as oracles, and indeed Micah, saying: 'who is a God like you, lifting away lawlessnesses and passing over injustices?' 29.3 And Peter in the Acts thus: 'and he charged us to preach to the people and to testify that he himself is the one marked out by God as judge of living and dead. To this one all the prophets bear witness, that everyone who believes into him receives forgiveness of sins through his name'. 29.4 We have him therefore spoken well of, marked out by [page number 34] God because of his saving becoming-man, in which he came 'to seek and to save the lost'; because of which also the saying 'for neither does the Father judge anyone, but he has given all the judgment to the Son' has been written; 29.5 and judge as being taken out from the creatures. 29.6 For the creature does not judge, but lies under law and judgment. 29.7 And again: 'this is the stone that was set at nothing by you the builders, that became head of the corner. And there is not in any other the salvation'. 29.8 But he also sends catholic letters the second time, having among other things about him this too: 'as his divine power has gifted us all things toward life and godliness through the full knowledge of the one who called us by his own glory and excellence, through which he has gifted to us the greatest and precious good tidings, so that through these you may become sharers of divine nature'. 29.9 Therefore James too said in general writings: 'one is the lawgiver and judge, the one able to save and to destroy'. 29.10 What need is there of a multitude of Scriptures for this, after all? And the Samaritans in John, the precise God-speaker, men of good mind, sending forth voices: 'for we ourselves', it says, 'have heard and know that this is truly the Saviour of the world, the Christ', the one saying, it says, gently: 'take heart, child, your sins have been forgiven you'. 30.ν [Chapter title:] About the Father, because of the equal honour of the Trinity, revealing the Son to us and drawing us toward him, and again the Son himself and the Holy Spirit bringing us to the Father. In the same place also about the confession of Peter, and that there is repentance. 30.1 For in order that the equality of honour in all things of the blessed Trinity may be shown through all things, the Father reveals to us his own Son and draws us through himself toward him and transfers [us] into his kingdom; 30.2 and again the Son and the Holy Spirit bring us to the God and Father. 30.3 For God would not have transferred us into one of another substance or greater, nor into things going down below, like sceptres from among his own. 30.4 At any rate the new has completed the old covenant, because of the faith into the Son and the divine Spirit. 30.5 And they say thus: God the Father in Isaiah to the Son: 'behold, proselytes will come to you through me, and will sojourn beside you, and will flee for refuge to you'; 30.6 and the Son in John: 'no one can come toward me unless the heavenly Father draw him, and I will raise him up on the last day'. 30.7 And again to Peter, who had said 'you are the Christ, the Son of the living God', he said: 'blessed are you, Peter Bar-Jonah, because flesh and blood did not reveal [it] to you, but my Father who is in the heavens. And I also say to you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and gates of Hades will not overpower it. And I will give you the keys of the heavens, and whatever you bind on the earth will be bound in the heavens, and whatever you loose on the earth will be loosed in the heavens'. 30.8 [the paragraph number ends the section; its text begins in the next section]
pass_b_english: For another saying of the same kind is spoken by the same prophet in the person of the Master: “Who is it that goes to law with me? Let him stand against me. And who is it that goes to law with me? Let him come near to me” (Isaiah 50:8). That is: if anyone has just things to say, as one fortified by his deeds, let him be set against me, since I wish it, and let him come near with his arguments.

Some, however, read it this way: “Who is it that goes to law with me? Let him stand over against”—that is, facing me and somewhere far off—“me,” as one who has no good provisions for the road, and is therefore unworthy to be compared with me and to touch the most pure judgment seat. For no one begrudges the worthy if they obtain good things; these have been prepared for them.
That the Son of God is “judge of the living and the dead,” granting forgiveness of sins, and that “there is salvation in no one else.”

For he himself is “the judge of the living and the dead” (Acts 10:42), that is, of the righteous and of sinners. He grants forgiveness of sins to those who believe in his name, and saves us by his own glory and gift. And “there is salvation in no one else” (Acts 4:12), since he is by nature merciful and Saviour, in nothing inferior to the merciful and saving God and Father. So the other Scriptures declare, and Micah in particular, saying: “Who is a God like you, taking away iniquities and passing over wrongs?” (Micah 7:18).

And Peter in the Acts, thus: “And he commanded us to preach to the people and to testify that he is the one appointed by God as judge of the living and the dead. To him all the prophets bear witness, that everyone who believes in him receives forgiveness of sins through his name” (Acts 10:42-43).

Here, then, we have him acclaimed and appointed by God because of his saving incarnation, in which he came “to seek and to save what was lost” (Luke 19:10). Because of it, too, it is written: “For the Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son” (John 5:22). And he is judge as one set apart from creatures; for a creature does not judge, but is subject to law and judgment.
And again: “This is the stone that was despised by you, the builders, which has become the head of the corner. And there is salvation in no one else” (Acts 4:11-12).

He also sends a second general letter, which among other things says this too about him: “As his divine power has given us all things that pertain to life and godliness, through the knowledge of him who called us by his own glory and excellence, through which he has given us the greatest and precious good tidings, so that through these you may become partakers of the divine nature” (2 Peter 1:3-4). That is why James too said in his general letter: “There is one lawgiver and judge, who is able to save and to destroy” (James 4:12).

But what need is there, after all, of a host of Scriptures for this? The Samaritans too, right-minded men, raise their voices in John, the exact spokesman of God: “For we ourselves,” they say, “have heard, and we know that this is truly the Saviour of the world, the Christ” (John 4:42); he who says gently, as Scripture says: “Take heart, child; your sins are forgiven” (Matthew 9:2).

That because the Trinity is equal in honour, the Father reveals the Son to us and draws us to him, and in turn the Son himself and the Holy Spirit bring us to the Father. Here also, on Peter’s confession, and that there is repentance.

For, so that the equal honour of the blessed Trinity in all things might be shown through everything, the Father reveals his own Son to us, draws us through himself to him, and transfers us into his kingdom (Colossians 1:13). And in turn the Son and the Holy Spirit bring us to God the Father. For God would not have transferred us to one of another substance, or greater, nor to lower powers handed down like sceptres from among his own. So the new covenant has brought the old to completion, through faith in the Son and the divine Spirit.

And they speak thus. God the Father says to the Son in Isaiah: “Behold, proselytes will come to you through me, and will dwell beside you, and will take refuge with you” (Isaiah 54:15 LXX). And the Son in John: “No one can come to me unless the heavenly Father draws him, and I will raise him up on the last day” (John 6:44).

And again, when Peter said, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God” (Matthew 16:16), he replied: “Blessed are you, Peter Bar-Jonah, for flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father who is in heaven. And I tell you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not overpower it. And I will give you the keys of the heavens; and whatever you bind on earth will be bound in the heavens, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in the heavens” (Matthew 16:17-19).
notes: Khazarzar; Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify

lemmas.gloss: the person (speaking role) of the Master
middle: go to law, dispute in court
one who speaks of God, spokesman of God
go down below; lower in rank

choices.issue: Old draft garbled, broke a quotation, printed edition numbers
choices.choice: Retranslated the whole section from the Greek. The old English printed 28.16, 28.17, '29.' and 29.1-29.8 inside the text, gave '(cf. Isaiah/Malachi allusion)' instead of a reference for Isaiah 50:8, garbled 28.16-28.17 ('to test the purest step', 'if they should happen to be of the good'), made Micah 7:18 'overcomes iniquities' (ὑπερβαίνων: passing over) and the Scriptures 'exhort' (χρησμῳδοῦσιν: declare), broke 2 Peter 1:3-4 into an unfinished fragment and a new, garbled sentence, made the Samaritans 'not reject the voices' (ἀφιέντων φωνάς: uttering words), and turned 'that there is repentance' in the chapter 30 title into 'that it is repentance'. References: Isaiah 50:8 supplied; Acts 10:42 widened to 10:42-43; 2 Peter 1:3-4, Acts 10:42 (29.1), Acts 4:12 (29.2) and Colossians 1:13 added; Isaiah 54:15 marked LXX. The fillers [letter] and [covenant] are gone: διαθήκη is in the Greek, and 'letter' is in γράμματα.

choices.english: in the person of the Master
choices.why: πρόσωπον in its exegetical sense: the speaking role the prophet takes. The old 'from the Lord's person' was unclear.
LXX Isaiah 50:8 uses the middle of κρίνω for a lawsuit; Didymus' gloss ('if anyone has just things to say') keeps the courtroom image, so 'judging me' (old draft) was wrong.

choices.english: “Let him stand over against”—that is, facing me and somewhere far off—“me”
choices.why: The alternative reading splits ἀντιστήτω into ἀντί with the genitive μου ('opposite me'); Didymus' gloss sits between the two words, so the English keeps the split.

choices.term: τοῖς γὰρ ἀξίοις ... οὐδεὶς φθόνος· αὐτοῖς γὰρ ἡτοίμασται
choices.english: For no one begrudges the worthy if they obtain good things; these have been prepared for them
choices.why: φθόνος here is grudging, as in the commonplace that the divine is without envy; 'these' renders the impersonal ἡτοίμασται with the good things as subject.

choices.term: κριτὴν δὲ ὡς ἐξῃρημένον τῶν κτισμάτων
choices.english: And he is judge as one set apart from creatures
choices.why: Elliptical clause continuing 'we have him'; English states the subject and verb. ἐξαιρέω (passive) means taken out of a class, not 'removed'.
Didymus' text of 2 Peter 1:4 reads εὐαγγέλματα where the New Testament has ἐπαγγέλματα (promises); translated as he has it.

choices.english: he who says gently, as Scripture says
choices.why: φησίν with no named subject introduces a scriptural citation; 'as Scripture says' makes clear the quoted words are Matthew's, not the Samaritans'.
Didymus has 'Peter' where Matthew has 'Simon'; kept as he quotes it.

choices.term: οὐδ' εἰς ὑποκατερχόμενα ὥσπερ σκῆπτρα τῶν ἑαυτοῦ
choices.english: nor to lower powers handed down like sceptres from among his own
choices.why: Neuter plural participle 'things that go down below', with the image of royal sceptres delegated to subordinates. 'Powers' is the least English needs for a neuter plural with no noun; not bracketed because the participle carries it.
Split words in the copy-text (ἁμαρ τιῶν, προ φῆται, ἀρε τῇ, τού των, κατισχύ σουσιν) read as single words; the page number '34' in 29.4 and the bare paragraph number '30.8' at the end are skipped.
